title: Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery
disposition_detail: Appeal dismissed under BCO 42-7; lower judgment suspended indefinitely because Pacific Presbytery failed to send a material part of the Record of the Case, an injury to Appellant that cannot be remedied; Pacific Presbytery rebuked and urged to take greater care to preserve, transcribe, and transmit all testimony in subsequent judicial proceedings.
first_summary: G. Rick Marshall appealed Pacific Presbytery after it failed to send a material part of the Record of the Case. The SJC suspended the lower judgment indefinitely, dismissed the appeal under BCO 42-7, and rebuked Pacific Presbytery, urging greater care in preserving, transcribing, and transmitting testimony. A concurrence suggested recording testimony or hiring a court reporter.
summary: G. Rick Marshall appealed Pacific Presbytery, which failed to transmit a material part of the Record of the Case, causing irremediable injury. The SJC did not reach the merits; it suspended the lower judgment indefinitely, dismissed the appeal under BCO 42-7, rebuked Pacific Presbytery, and urged greater care in preserving, transcribing, and transmitting testimony. Dismissal therefore did not leave the challenged judgment enforceable. A separate concurrence suggested recording testimony or hiring a court reporter and questioned imprudent prosecutions.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2013-12, Marshall v. Pacific Presbytery, appeal decided Oct. 16, 2014; adopted 18 concurring, 0 dissenting, 0 recused, 0 abstaining, 6 absent (lines 13–28).
evidence_notes.dispute: Appellant G. Rick Marshall appealed Pacific Presbytery; the lower court failed to send up a material part of the Record of the Case, causing injury to Appellant that cannot be remedied (lines 15, 19–21).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC suspended the lower judgment indefinitely and dismissed under BCO 42-7; it rebuked Pacific Presbytery and urged greater care to preserve, transcribe, and transmit all testimony (lines 19–24). The stated reason was the lower court's material and unremediable failure to transmit the record (lines 19–21).
evidence_notes.qualifications: No merits ruling on the appeal; the challenged judgment was suspended indefinitely, so dismissal did not leave it enforceable. RE Howard Donahoe's concurrence separately suggested recording testimony or hiring a court reporter and questioned imprudent prosecutions; that is not the adopted majority reasoning (lines 32–61).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None. The concurrence cites Case 2011-15 Hahn v. Philadelphia Metro West only in a footnote for a separate point (line 61).
